scams.name: The Siena–Firenze Mirror Scam (Truffa dello Specchietto)
scams.description: Siena News' investigation "Siena–Firenze: ecco la truffa dello specchietto" documents the technique exactly: "La tecnica seguita da questi personaggi è sempre quella, simulare un danneggiamento (quasi sempre lo specchietto laterale) della propria auto" — the same con, same script, same stretch of road, hitting car after car. Radio Siena TV's reporting nails the tourist-targeting: "Truffa dello specchietto ad un turista tedesco, nei guai un 34enne" describes a German driver who was flagged down, accused of breaking the scammer's mirror, and pressured to pay on the roadside before the police arrested the 34-year-old perpetrator. A separate Radio Siena TV piece — "Carabiniere fuori servizio sventa nuova truffa dello specchietto e incastra il malvivente" — describes an off-duty Carabiniere thwarting a mirror-scam attempt and arresting the perpetrator on the spot. A third Radio Siena TV arrest — "Truffa dello specchietto: nomade colto sul fatto"; the getaway car, a white VW Golf, was seized and matched descriptions from multiple previous reports. The Reddit thread — where Italian drivers themselves warn visitors — lists the defensive playbook that Siena and Tuscany travelers need to know: "Keep doors locked. Only open windows a crack, or not at all. Drive off immediately if you hear such a far-…" A separate traveler thread documents a driver whose Siena hotel was at the border of a ZTL and who was bombarded with fake-damage demands on the approach. Keep rental-car doors locked and windows up on the entire Firenze–Siena/SS2 stretch, especially near lay-bys and petrol-station approaches; if another driver signals damage, do not pull onto the hard shoulder — continue to the next exit or petrol station and park in view of CCTV. Never pay cash on the roadside (Italian law requires a Constatazione Amichevole / CAI joint report, and your rental insurance is void if you settle privately). Call 112 before discussing anything; photograph your mirror at rental pickup so you have a time-stamped before-shot that kills the bluff instantly.
scams.avoidance: Keep rental-car doors locked and windows up on the Firenze–Siena / SS2 stretch. If another driver signals damage, do not pull onto the hard shoulder — continue to the next exit or petrol station. Never pay cash on the roadside; Italian law requires a joint accident report (CAI) and rental insurance is void if you settle privately. Call 112 before discussing anything. Photograph your mirror at rental pickup for a time-stamped 'before' shot.
scams.location: Siena–Firenze raccordo (E78), SS2 Cassia, A1 autostrada exit corridor to Siena, lay-bys on all approach roads
scams.tldr: The "Truffa dello Specchietto" mirror scam works the Siena–Firenze raccordo (E78), SS2 Cassia, and A1 autostrada exit corridor — typically a white VW Golf or small Fiat pulls alongside, the driver gestures at your side mirror, then at the next lay-by produces a pre-broken mirror and demands €150–€300 cash "to avoid the insurance hassle"; Radio Siena TV has documented multiple arrests of these crews (a 23-year-old fake-mirror perpetrator, an off-duty Carabiniere catch, a nomade arrest with a white VW Golf seized) — keep doors locked, drive to the next exit not the lay-by, never settle on the roadside, call 112 (Carabinieri) before discussing.

scams.name: ZTL Camera Fines on Rental Cars
scams.description: Urbanaccessregulations.eu's Siena page is unambiguous: "L'ingresso non autorizzato in una ZTL è punibile con pesanti multe. La sanzione prevista è di circa 100 euro (87 euro di multa più spese amministrative)." Sigerico's official explainer adds the less-obvious rule that "con lo stesso permesso ZTL è vietato sostare nel parcheggio in struttura con più veicoli contemporaneamente; sostare nel parcheggio in struttura e…" — meaning even a legitimate ZTL permit doesn't cover multi-day parking abuse. Radio Siena TV's "Ganasce e multe per le auto in ztl" story documents the enforcement tempo: vigili urbani booted ten unauthorized ZTL vehicles in a single afternoon patrol and wrote tickets on all of them. The Rick Steves Travel Forum thread "Car Rental Siena — Caveat Emptor" is the foreigner's-perspective warning that corroborates the Italian-press reality: drivers report receiving ZTL violation letters four months after return, by which point the rental company has already debited the fine plus a fee from the card on file. A general Italian travel guide — italybeyondtheobvious.com's "5 Easy Ways to Get Italian ZTL Fines and How to Avoid One" — confirms that if the car is rented, the rental company adds its own handling charge on top of the comune fine. The Facebook Tuscany travel-tips thread "ZTL zone fines in Siena" makes the timeline plain: "Yes, you will be fined. You'll get the ticket in three or four months in the mail. There's a good chance it will be overdue when you receive it," at which point the €87 base has often grown with late-payment surcharges. This isn't a scam run by an Italian on a tourist — but because every third-party blog and rental counter skips the warning, it functions like one. Park outside the walls at Parcheggio Il Campo (Viale del Stadio), Parcheggio Il Duomo, Parcheggio Santa Caterina, or Parcheggio San Francesco — all 5–10 minutes walking from Piazza del Campo. If your hotel is inside the walls, email the hotel your plate number and arrival time at least 48 hours in advance so they can register your plate with the Comune di Siena before you pass the gate. Refuse rental-company "admin fees" without a copy of the original comune.siena.it violation notice (EU consumer law requires they show the underlying fine), and never ignore a ZTL letter — pay within 5 days for the "sconto" half-discount.
scams.avoidance: Leave rental cars at paid lots outside the walls — Parcheggio Il Campo (Viale del Stadio), Parcheggio Il Duomo, Parcheggio Santa Caterina, or Parcheggio San Francesco — and walk in. If staying at a hotel inside the ZTL, email plate and arrival time 48 hours ahead so the hotel can register it with Comune di Siena before the gate. Never ignore a ZTL letter — pay within 5 days for the 'sconto' early-payment discount. Refuse rental admin fees without a copy of the underlying comune.siena.it notice.
scams.location: All historic-center ZTL gates — Porta Camollia, Porta San Marco, Porta Tufi, Porta Romana, Porta Pispini, Porta Ovile — and the entire walled old town
scams.tldr: Siena's UNESCO old town is a camera-enforced ZTL whose gate signs (Porta Camollia, San Marco, Tufi, Romana, Pispini, Ovile) are in Italian and placed after the GPS point of no return — Google Maps routinely routes hotel-bound rentals through them. Each entry is €87 base + €40–€60 rental-company "admin fee" — combined ~€100–€200 per entry, fines arriving 3–4 months later (often past the 5-day "sconto" half-discount window), and rental companies have already debited the card on file. Park outside the walls (Parcheggio Il Campo, Il Duomo, Santa Caterina, San Francesco — all 5–10 min walk to Piazza del Campo).

scams.name: The Palio Ticket & "Balcony Access" Scalper Scam
scams.description: The Comune di Siena's official "Palio" portal ("Palio, formulati gli addebiti di contestazione delle Carriere 2025") explains the race's tight regulatory framework: the Deputati della Festa produce a written relazione after each Palio under article 92, comma 3, and the Carriere (race results) carry formal legal weight — which is why the ticketing ecosystem is so controlled and why online "independent" resale of bleacher seats is always suspect. Palco (bleacher) tickets and balcony (balconi) seats are sold each year by the licensed hotels ringing the Piazza (such as Palazzo Ravizza or hotels facing Piazza del Campo), by individual Contrade to their members and guests, and by a handful of official historic-center agencies — anything on eBay, Viagogo, StubHub, or unbranded "Siena Palio Tickets 2026" websites is almost always either a scalped price (real seat, marked up 3–5×) or a fully fake listing. Italian media and Siena-focused travel forums have documented year after year that scalpers work the Piazza perimeter in the 48 hours before each Palio, selling "bleacher access" wristbands that collapse at the actual entrance check. A secondary pattern: predatory restaurants and hotels on Piazza del Campo advertising "Palio package rooms" at 5–10× normal rates for July 1–3 and August 15–17, often bundled with a low-quality bleacher seat the traveler could have booked directly. A Corriere Fiorentino archive piece from 2023 even documented a Florentine man arrested on Piazza del Campo during a Palio for filming women's private parts — a reminder that the dense crowds in the inner ring are also opportunistic-crime scenes in their own right. The Palio happens twice; the scam has twelve months a year to reboot. The free inner-ring standing area (il Campo / la conchiglia) is still the purest Palio experience — arrive by 2pm with water and sun protection, and expect to stay standing until the race finishes around 7:30pm. For bleacher (palchi) or balcony (balconi) seats, book through a verifiably Siena-licensed hotel that owns a palco (Palazzo Ravizza, NH Siena, Grand Hotel Continental Siena) and get a named seat assignment in writing before paying. Never wire money to a "Palio tickets" website that cannot produce a Comune di Siena registration number or a Contrada affiliation; if a "wristband pass" is offered on the Piazza day-of, walk away (legitimate bleacher entry is checked against a named list plus ID).
scams.avoidance: The free inner-ring standing area remains the purest experience — arrive by 2pm, bring water and sun protection. For bleacher/balcony seats, book through a verifiably Siena-licensed Piazza-del-Campo hotel (Palazzo Ravizza, NH Siena, Grand Hotel Continental Siena) with a named seat assignment in writing. Never wire money to 'Palio ticket' sites without a Comune di Siena registration number or Contrada affiliation. Walk away from day-of wristband sellers — legitimate entry is checked against a named list plus ID. Carry minimum cash and one card in the inner-ring crowd.
scams.location: Piazza del Campo inner-ring, outer-ring palchi/balconi, surrounding Contrada streets during July 2 and August 16 Palios
scams.tldr: Siena's Palio (July 2 / August 16) inner-ring standing area is genuinely free but requires arriving by 2pm; outer bleacher (palchi) and balcony seats are tightly controlled — sold by Contrade, licensed Piazza-del-Campo hotels (Palazzo Ravizza, NH Siena, Grand Hotel Continental Siena), and a handful of registered agencies. eBay/Viagogo/StubHub/unbranded "Siena Palio Tickets 2026" sites are 3–5× scalper markups or outright fakes, and Piazza-perimeter wristband sellers in the 24–48 hours before the race collapse at the actual entrance check; book direct through a Comune-registered hotel with a named seat assignment in writing.

scams.name: The Piazza del Campo Coperto & "Pesce al Etto" Trap
scams.description: A TripAdvisor review of Il Campo restaurant on the east side of Piazza del Campo (Piazza del Campo 50, 53100 Siena) puts the markup directly: "Ps. se vendete una pizza a 14€ almeno compratela buona, non da 2€" — a 14€ pizza the reviewer judged worth 2€. The mechanisms follow the Italian-tourist-trap playbook that applies from Rome to Venice and is actively practiced on Piazza del Campo: an unmarked per-person coperto line, often above €3.50; an "optional" 10–15% servizio applied automatically to foreign cards; unrequested pane, acqua, or antipasti landing on the table; and fish or steak priced "al etto" (per 100g) that arrives as a 400–600g portion at 5× the expected price. Italian law requires every restaurant to post a menu with prices in public view outside the door — if no menu is posted or the fish/meat has no per-unit price, it is legally non-compliant and a near-certain trap. A separate pattern on Piazza del Campo: "menu turistico" boards displaying three glossy courses for €20–€28 that unbundle into five lines on the bill by the time they hit the printer. Sienese food is genuinely worth eating — pici, pappardelle al cinghiale, panforte, ricciarelli, brodo di pollo con cappelletti — but not inside the Piazza perimeter. Ristorante Spadaforte (est. 1988, on Piazza del Campo) and Osteria da Gano (on Via di Pantaneto near Piazza del Campo) are examples of long-running places locals still vouch for, but they are the minority on the ring. Walk 2–5 minutes off Piazza del Campo to Via dei Termini, Via di Stalloreggi, Via del Porrione, or the San Martino and Salicotto contrade for locals-priced osterias with handwritten daily menus. Photograph the outside-posted menu before sitting down — Italian law (L. 287/1991) requires posted prices, and a missing menu means leave. Ask "mi conferma il coperto e se c'è servizio?" at seating (a Sienese trattoria confirms €1.50–€2.50 and no automatic servizio); if fish or steak is "al etto," ask "quanto verrà al peso?" before ordering. Trust Google Maps reviews sorted by Italian / Most Recent — a venue rated 4.5+ by Italian reviewers is authentic, and the reverse signals a tourist trap.
scams.avoidance: Walk 2–5 minutes off the Piazza — Via dei Termini, Via di Stalloreggi, Via del Porrione, San Martino/Salicotto contrada streets have locals-priced osterias. Photograph the outside menu before sitting (Italian law requires it). At seating ask 'mi conferma il coperto e se c'è servizio?'. For fish/steak al etto demand a weight quote and stated total before ordering. Trust Google reviews in Italian sorted Most Recent over English reviews.
scams.location: Restaurants on the curve of Piazza del Campo facing the Torre del Mangia; Via di Città, Via dei Rinaldini, Via Banchi di Sotto, Via Pantaneto
scams.tldr: Piazza del Campo outdoor restaurants and the immediate side streets (Via di Città, Via dei Rinaldini, Via Banchi di Sotto, Via Pantaneto) pad bills with €4-per-person coperto, automatically-applied "optional 10–15% servizio" on foreign cards, unrequested bread/water/antipasti, and pesce/carne priced "al etto" (per 100g) that arrives at 5× the displayed unit price; Italian law (L. 287/1991) requires posted menus visible outside, so leave any venue without prices, and walk 2–5 min off the Piazza to Via dei Termini, Via di Stalloreggi, Via del Porrione, or the San Martino/Salicotto contrade for honest osterias.

scams.name: The Finti Ambulanti Rom & Piazza Gramsci Pickpocket Corridor
scams.description: La Nazione Siena's reporting "Finti ambulanti Rom e mendicanti, scattano i controlli in centro" documents the problem in the shopkeepers' own words: "Commercianti ed esercenti: 'Molestano e derubano i turisti'. Il vicesindaco Corsi: 'Ordine di servizio, più vigili nelle zone affollate'" — local business owners reported to the Siena comune that fake street-vendors and beggars were harassing and robbing tourists, and the deputy mayor issued an order bringing more municipal police into the crowded zones. Siena News' cronaca archive documents one striking variant: "Sale sul bus e strappa una collana ad una turista, arrestato 23enne" — a 23-year-old boarded a bus, snatched a necklace from a tourist's neck, and was arrested after the Questura di Siena operations room took the emergency call at 9:15am. The walk from Piazza Gramsci (where intercity buses from Florence arrive) into the centro historico passes through exactly the "zone affollate" La Nazione flags, and the day-tripping tourist load — typically arriving 10am–11am, lingering 4–6 hours, departing late afternoon — concentrates vulnerable targets into a predictable 600-metre funnel. The corridor also hosts active "finto finanziere" shakedowns (see Scam #7). Patterns to expect: fake "deaf-mute petition" clipboards pressed against your chest while a partner opens your pack pocket; staged stumble-and-apologize bumps on the Via Banchi di Sopra narrowing; and Via di Città souvenir stalls where the shopkeeper distracts while a "customer" beside you reaches into your bag. Wear your day-pack on your chest (not your back) on the full Piazza Gramsci → Piazza del Campo corridor and around the Duomo. Keep wallet, passport, and phone in an inside zipped pocket or a flat pouch under your shirt — never in an outer day-pack pocket or back trouser pocket. Respond to any "signature," "petition," or bracelet approach with a firm "no, grazie" and keep walking — do not stop, do not look at the clipboard. If you feel a brush or tug, check your bag/phone/wallet immediately and shout "ladri!" — La Nazione Siena documents that on-foot vigili now actively patrol the "zone affollate" and response time is short.
scams.avoidance: Wear day-packs on your chest, not your back, on the full Piazza Gramsci → Piazza del Campo corridor and around the Duomo. Keep wallet/passport/phone in an inside zip pocket or a flat pouch under your shirt. Respond to any 'signature,' 'petition,' or bracelet approach with a firm 'no, grazie' and keep walking. On Siena city buses, keep valuables under your outer layer and one hand on the bag strap. Shout 'ladri!' on contact — vigili patrol the 'zone affollate' per the comune's order.
scams.location: Piazza Gramsci bus station, Via dei Termini, Via Banchi di Sopra, Via di Città, Via del Capitano, Piazza Matteotti, Porta Camollia
scams.tldr: The 600-meter Piazza Gramsci → Piazza del Campo corridor (Via dei Termini, Via Banchi di Sopra) is Siena's peak pickpocket funnel — concentrating the 10am–11am Florence-day-tripper arrival load in the predictable "zone affollate" La Nazione documented; "finti ambulanti" press petitions or bracelets to your chest while a partner unzips your day-pack, "lost tourists" position to block your bag-side view, and a 23-year-old necklace-snatcher arrested at 9:15am after boarding a Siena bus is on Siena News' record; wear day-pack on chest, not back, on the full corridor.

scams.name: The Canceled Wine-Tour / Fake Tuscany Day-Trip Operator
scams.description: TripAdvisor reviews of Siena-listed Chianti-tour operators document the pattern directly. One traveler wrote: "Apparently there is a scam going on with tour operators here in Siena. I had booked 3 wine tours as each one kept getting canceled the day before the tour," leaving the traveler repeatedly without a day's activity and forced to rebook on no notice. A second reviewer documents the other variant: "Warning this is a scam! Bought a 'small group tour' max 8 people, ended up being over 40 people. Bad experience. False advertisement, customer service…" A third review of the same operator's Florence-to-Siena Vespa Chianti tour is emphatic: "Do NOT book a trip with this company! We tried the full day Vespa tour in Chianti. We stayed in Siena where the organization would pick us up at 9.30." Still another: "These thieves who masquerade as a tour company scammed my friend and I out of 150 euros! They arranged to pick us up at our apartment, they never came." A separate CruiseCritic Italy Ports thread titled "Tuscany Tour Fraud" collects similar reports from cruisers doing day-trips up from Livorno. Reddit traveler reports's "Renting a Car in Tuscany — Avoid this trap!" thread surfaces a related variant on rental-counter upsells: "This is not a trap — this is a single scumbag employee trying to rip you off. It happens all the time and especially with rental car places where…" the operator uses a Siena pickup address to bundle in damage-waiver and fuel charges that weren't in the booking. The common thread: unlicensed or under-regulated operators selling Siena-originating Tuscany tours who ghost, oversell, or bait-and-switch. Book Siena-originating Tuscany day-tours through Viator or GetYourGuide only with operators having 500+ reviews and 4.6+ average — and read the most recent 1-star reviews first. Prefer guides holding a Regione Toscana guida turistica abilitazione license (legitimate operators list the license number on their website). Pay by credit card (not wire transfer or PayPal Friends & Family) for Visa/Mastercard/Amex chargeback rights, and screenshot the group-size cap and exact pickup address in writing before paying. For Chianti specifically, book direct with a named estate (Castello di Verrazzano, Castello di Ama, Fattoria dei Barbi in Montalcino) and use Uber or NCC from Siena — cheaper and verifiable.
scams.avoidance: Book only via Viator/GetYourGuide with operators having 500+ reviews at 4.6+ average — read recent 1-stars first. Prefer licensed Regione Toscana guida turistica with a posted license number. Pay by credit card (Visa/Mastercard/Amex) for chargeback rights; never wire or PayPal F&F. Screenshot group-size cap and named pickup address before paying. For Chianti, book directly with named estates (Castello di Verrazzano, Castello di Ama, Fattoria dei Barbi) and drive or NCC from Siena.
scams.location: Unlicensed Siena-pickup tour operators advertised on Viator, GetYourGuide, TripAdvisor Experiences; Piazza Gramsci/San Domenico street agents
scams.tldr: Unlicensed Siena-originating "small group max 8" Chianti / Montalcino / Val d'Orcia / San Gimignano / Pienza day-tour operators ghost the morning of (no refund) or oversell to 40+ in a converted bus visiting operator-owned bulk-tasting shops; TripAdvisor and CruiseCritic threads collect dozens of "canceled," "never showed," and "bait-and-switch" reports — book only 4.6+ rated operators with 500+ reviews on Viator/GetYourGuide, prefer guides holding a Regione Toscana abilitazione license, and pay by credit card for chargeback.

scams.name: The "Finto Finanziere" Fake-Officer Cash Shakedown
scams.description: An April 10, 2026 local Siena news bulletin — "Siena, truffa del 'finto finanziere': denunciato quarantaduenne" — reports the indictment of a 42-year-old running this exact play in the centro storico. The archive on Ansa's Tuscany desk includes multiple related incidents — "Sventata truffa del 'finto [finanziere]'…" — confirming the MO recurs. Radio Siena TV's archive similarly flags recurring "anti-truffa anziani" PSAs from the Siena Questura warning specifically about fake-officer approaches; the comune has distributed a "vademecum contro le truffe" to elderly residents, and the warning apparatus exists precisely because the fake-officer pattern is chronic. The variant targeting tourists combines badge-flash with a "tassa turistica" / "imposta di soggiorno" pretext: the real Siena tourism tax is collected by your hotel at check-in or check-out (rates set by deliberazione comunale, typically €1.50–€5 per person per night depending on accommodation class) — it is never collected on the street by a passing "ispettore." A related pattern on Siena News' archive is the "truffa del bancomat" / bancomat-attack cluster — professional teams targeting ATMs and elderly victims — which uses the same authority-impersonation playbook: "Veri e propri assalti ai bancomat, questo il modus operandi con cui avevano terrorizzato il Centro Italia." Tourists hit by this scam typically lose €50–€300 plus whatever card data is photographed during the fake-inspection. Real Italian police (Guardia di Finanza, Carabinieri, Polizia di Stato, Polizia Locale) do not conduct cash-inspections of tourists on the street — anyone claiming to do so is a scammer. Refuse to show your wallet, phone, passport, or cash to any plain-clothes "officer" outside an official station; say clearly "andiamo al commissariato" (let's go to the police station — a real officer will agree, a scammer will vanish). Call 112 (general emergencies) or 117 (Guardia di Finanza) on the spot and stay on the line while the caller identifies himself. Pay the Siena tourist tax (imposta di soggiorno, €1.50–€5/person/night by accommodation class) only to your hotel at check-in or check-out, and keep the hotel receipt — never pay it to anyone on the street.
scams.avoidance: Real Italian police do not conduct street cash-inspections of tourists. Refuse to show wallet, phone, passport or cash to any plain-clothes 'officer' outside an official station. Say 'andiamo al commissariato' — a real officer will agree, a scammer will vanish. Call 112 or 117 (Guardia di Finanza) on the spot and stay on the line. Pay the Siena tourist tax only to your hotel with a named receipt.
scams.location: Historic-center streets around Piazza del Campo, the Duomo, Banchi di Sopra/Sotto, Palio viewing perimeter on Palio weekends
scams.tldr: "Finto finanziere" fake-officer scammers work Siena's historic-center streets around Piazza del Campo, the Duomo, Banchi di Sopra/Sotto, and (per 2026 reports) the Palio viewing perimeter — flashing what looks like a Guardia di Finanza badge, claiming counterfeit cash or "tassa di soggiorno" owed on the street, and offering to "verify" your wallet contents; an April 10, 2026 Siena news bulletin documents the indictment of a 42-year-old, and Italian police never inspect tourist wallets on the street — refuse, say "andiamo al commissariato," and call 112 or 117 (Guardia di Finanza).
